question: How does the Śiva-state flash forth, and whence the numbered divisions?
premises: In the Īśa domain the Mantreśa class abides, and in the most auspicious abode stands devotion to that Lord.
Each prior stage therein discloses its own knower-measure order, so that with no other knower the ever-one self-luminous Śiva-state flashes forth.
From the Mantreśa-Īśas however come divisions by number: three, five, seven, nine, three.
inference: The one self-luminous Śiva-state emerges through the ordered knower-system, then differentiates into numbered Mantreśa groups.
uncertainties: Exact syntactic joints of the long compounds left open.
The referents of the 3-5-7-9-3 counts read as group-numbers, specific groups unidentified.
plain_english: In the Īśa domain abides the class of Mantreśas; now, in the most auspicious abode, devotion to that Lord — and each prior stage therein reveals its own order of knower and measure — so that, with no other knower, the self-luminous state of Śiva flashes forth ever one; yet from the Mantreśa-Īśas issue divisions numbered three, five, seven, nine, and three.
